title: studio: the flow inspector refuses a valid text envelope in a record node's fields (judges it as an assignment value), after #34062
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pmEYLVFDcQ1Z1CS8H

Filing gate: ① a user-visible defect with a named location. A follow-up that PR #34438 (#34062, p1) owes before the release an app installs. It was found by review#1 as should-fix S2 in contract record 6924979595 on #34438. `reach:` read from code on the PR head `b585364d`, not driven in a browser.

## What happens

Once #34438 lands, a create_record / update_record node's `fields` value can be a text envelope that the platform translates at write time (ruling B, 6913660232). The Studio inspector does not know this:
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeConfigField.tsx`, in the `keyValue` case, passes no `valueRefusal` for a record node's `fields`.
- So `FlowKeyValueField` judges each cell with `valueEnvelopeRefusal`, which is `AssignmentValueSchema` (`flow-value-envelope.ts:128`).

A valid text envelope is therefore shown with the refusal "`template` and `cron` envelopes have no meaning here … write one CEL concatenation", the very spelling the ruling rejects. The row is kept, so nothing is lost on save, but the author is told that a correct value is wrong.

## Expected

The record node's `fields` cells are judged with `FlowRecordFieldValueSchema`, the schema #34438 publishes, so a text envelope reads as valid and an invalid value still gets the right refusal.

## Acceptance

- The inspector passes the record-field judge for create_record / update_record `fields`.
- A UI test shows a text envelope with no refusal, and a control shows a malformed value still refused.

Priority p1, as part of delivering #34062. Ships in the same release as #34438, or the release after it at the latest.
